text:
Alice: Heads-up — planning schema migration for payments.transactions tonight at 01:00 UTC. add nullable column `processed_at` + small backfill. change window 01:00-02:00 UTC.
Ben: ok, what's the rollback plan if backfill spikes locks?
Alice: primary rollback is: 1) abort backfill, 2) pause write traffic via feature-flag to fallback codepath, 3) run reverse migration to drop column if needed.
Carla: can we avoid long locks by doing chunked backfill with a row-range predicate? I can run a small patch to the backfill worker for jittered pauses.
Dave: agree on chunking. also want a preflight to sample top-10 tenants and run backfill there to estimate per-tenant latency.
Eve: add to checklist: update release notes + ops runbook with exact FRs and who pagers. I'll own release notes.
Ben: deploybot, queue migration for 2024-09-12T01:00Z window and pin db-mig v2.7.3 on the canary group please.
deploybot: Migration queued by @ben for 2024-09-12T01:00Z (db-mig v2.7.3). Canary group: 10% tenants. ETA backfill estimate: 15m/sample.
Alice: runbook items: 
- preflight sample run at 00:20 UTC (Carla)
- canary launch at 01:00 (10% tenants)
- monitor table locks, p99 latency, and write error rate (SLO: <0.5% errors)
- abort criteria: any sustained lock wait >5s on primary or error rate >1% for 5m
- rollback steps written in playbook (see snippet)

Alice: Playbook snippet:
```
# abort flow
POST /feature-flag/payments_backfill_pause true  # toggles code to skip backfill writes
kubectl -n prod exec backfill-worker -- pkill -f backfill || true
psql -c "-- run only if we confirmed backfill aborted
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE '%UPDATE payments.transactions%';"
# reverse migration (manual): rails db:rollback STEP=1
```

Carla: I'll implement chunking with randomized sleep and wire it behind a flag so we can toggle faster if canary looks good.
Dave: I can do preflight and collect latency histograms, will post results in this thread.
Ben: question: do we need a quick-read replica promotion plan if primary becomes unsafe? would prefer read-only fallback vs full rollback.
Alice: yes — fallback option B: promote read-replica for reads and enable degraded mode for writers (queue writes to kafka). Only use if abort + reverse migration would be too risky. Marked as escalation path in runbook.
Eve: Release notes draft: "Added nullable processed_at to payments.transactions to help downstream latency metrics. Backfill runs during maintenance window; no schema change to primary keys." I'll DM you a link to the draft for signoff.
deploybot: Canary started at 01:00Z — 10% tenant slice. Monitoring hooks live.
Dave: preflight done (00:20): sample 10k rows, avg backfill row time 1.2ms, peak lock wait 0.3s. Sharing histograms: https://internal.ops/charts/4132456789
Ben: looks safe from preflight numbers.
Carla: chunking flag is ready to flip if we see tail spikes.
Alice: Decision: proceed with canary. If we hit abort criteria, we follow playbook and escalate to fallback replica promotion. I'll post a final confirm at 00:50 UTC.
Eve: noted, prepping release notes and pager roster.
Alice: final: canary GO at 01:00. tagging on-call: @dave @carla.
